study type: Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) with a cost-effectiveness analysis
cohort: The study recruited 543 women undergoing caesarean section in Poland.
finding: The bacterial-binding dressing group had significantly lower SSI rates (1.8% vs 5.2%, p=0.04) and resulted in a cost saving of PS24.27 to PS119 per patient compared to standard of care.
mod_finding: N/A (the study was conducted on women post-caesarean section, so mode of birth was not a variable being compared).
